source: control-plane replies whose media-typed body is empty still carry content-type (MockServerHttpResponseToFullHttpResponse.setHeaders checks the body's content type, not its length)

tcp.text:
PUT /mockserver/retrieve?type=ACTIVE_EXPECTATIONS&format=java HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 0
Connection: close

steps.note: no expectations: the Java writer writes nothing, and withBody("", MediaType) still names application/java, after connection, with content-length 0

tcp.text:
PUT /mockserver/retrieve?type=RECORDED_EXPECTATIONS&format=java HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 0
Connection: close

steps.note: nothing recorded: the same empty Java body with its media type

tcp.text:
PUT /mockserver/retrieve?type=REQUESTS&format=curl HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 0
Connection: close

steps.note: no requests: the cURL writer writes only its closing newline, text/plain

tcp.text:
PUT /mockserver/files/store HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 38
Connection: close

{"name":"empty-0874.txt","content":""}

PUT /mockserver/files/retrieve HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 25
Connection: close

{"name":"empty-0874.txt"}

steps.note: contrast: an empty binary body names no media type, so no content-type
